radiology_report:
Spaarne Gasthuis (Haarlem)
Radiology Dept
Date: 28 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (12.87 ng/mL) with prior biopsy-proven prostate cancer. Request for staging and lesion characterisation.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume is 52.0 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal, ill-defined hypointense lesion in the mid-peripheral zone, right side, measuring approximately 14 mm in greatest dimension. The lesion shows marked restricted diffusion on DWI (high signal on b=1400) with corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) sequences demonstrate early, intense enhancement of the lesion. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy is seen.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the mid-peripheral zone, right side.
PSA density: 0.25 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT2a.
csPCa predicted probability 0.85843223.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 11.5 ng/mL, a significant rise from the previous year. A transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed, which revealed prostate cancer. The patient was referred to urology for further management discussion. He was advised to monitor symptoms and follow up in 6 months.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (Aug 2023): The submitted tissue fragments show acinar adenocarcinoma, partly with papillary, cribriform areas, partly invasive cribriform growth. The Gleason score is 4+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 3. Cribriform pattern and intraductal carcinoma (IDC-P) are present. Perineural invasion is identified. The tumour is located in the mid-prostate, right side.

Summary trajectory: The histological findings remain consistent across the available biopsy timepoint, showing high-grade disease with aggressive morphological features.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 5.
